column1: The first students to study alternative medicine at university level in Australia began their four-year, full-time course at the University of Technology Sydney, in early 1994.
column2: 澳大利亚首批在大学阶段学习替代医学的学生于1994年初在悉尼科技大学开始了为期四年的全日制课程。

column1: Their course covered, among other therapies, acupuncture.
column2: 他们的课程包括针灸等多种疗法。

column1: The theory they learnt is based on the traditional Chinese explanation of this ancient healing art that it can regulate the flow of‘Qi’ or energy through pathways in the body.
column2: 他们所学到的理论基于中国传统医学对这种古老治疗方法的解释，该理论认为，这种治疗方法能够调节体内‘气’或能量的流动。

column1: This course reflects how far some alternative therapies have come in their struggle for acceptance by the medical establishment.
column2: 这门课程反映了某些替代疗法在争取医学界认可过程中所取得的进展。

column1: Australia has been unusual in the Western world in having a very conservative attitude to natural or alternative therapies, according to Dr Paul Laver, a lecturer in Public Health at the University of Sydney.
column2: 根据悉尼大学公共卫生学讲师保罗·拉弗博士的说法，在西方世界中，澳大利亚对于自然疗法或替代疗法的态度相当保守。

column1: ‘We’ve had a tradition of doctors being fairly powerful and I guess they are pretty loath to allow any pretenders to their position to come into it.’
column2: ‘我们有一套传统，认为医生应该拥有相当大的权力。我想，他们肯定不愿意让那些试图篡夺其职位的人上台。’

column1: In many other industrialised countries, orthodox and alternative medicine have worked‘hand in glove’ for years.
column2: 在许多其他工业化国家，正统医学与替代医学已长期密切合作。

column1: In Europe, only orthodox doctors can prescribe herbal medicine.
column2: 在欧洲，只有正统的医生才能开具草药处方。

column1: In Germany, plant remedies account for 10% of the national turnover of pharmaceuticals.
column2: 在德国，植物制剂占该国制药行业总营业额的10%。

column1: Americans made more visits to alternative therapists than to orthodox doctors in 1990, and each year they spend about $US12 billion on therapies that have not been scientifically tested.
column2: 1990年，美国人去替代治疗师的次数多于去正统医生的次数，每年在未经科学检验的疗法上花费约120亿美元。

column1: Disenchantment with orthodox medicine has seen the popularity of alternative therapies in Australia climb steadily during the past 20 years.
column2: 在过去20年里，由于人们对传统医学的失望，替代疗法的受欢迎程度在澳大利亚逐渐上升。

column1: In a 1983 national health survey, 1.9% of people said they had contacted a chiropractor, naturopath, osteopath, acupuncturist or herbalist in the two weeks prior to the survey.
column2: 在1983年的一项全国健康调查中，有1.9%的人表示，在调查前两周内曾咨询过脊椎按摩师、自然疗法医生、骨疗师、针灸师或草药医师。

column1: By 1990, this figure had risen to 2.6% of the population.
column2: 到1990年，这一比例已上升至人口的2.6%。

column1: The 550,000 consultations with alternative therapists reported in the 1990 survey represented about an eighth of the total number of consultations with medically qualified personnel covered by the survey, according to Dr Laver and colleagues writing in the Australian Journal of Public Health in 1993.
column2: 根据拉弗博士在1993年发表于《澳大利亚公共卫生杂志》上的研究，1990年调查中记录的55万次替代疗法咨询次数，约占当时接受医学专业咨询总人数的一八分之一。

column1: ‘A better educated and less accepting public has become disillusioned with the experts in general, and increasingly sceptical about science and empirically based knowledge,’ they said.
column2: ‘受教育程度更高、接受能力更弱的公众，已经对专家们产生了怀疑，他们对科学以及基于实证的知识也持越来越怀疑的态度，’他们如此说道。

column1: ‘The high standing of professionals, including doctors, has been eroded as a consequence.’
column2: 专业人士，包括医生，其地位已遭侵蚀。

column1: Rather than resisting or criticising this trend, increasing numbers of Australian doctors, particularly younger ones, are forming group practices with alternative therapists or taking courses themselves, particularly in acupuncture and herbalism.
column2: 越来越多的澳大利亚医生，尤其是年轻医生，并没有抵制或批评这一趋势，而是与不同的治疗师合作开展集体诊疗服务，或者自己学习相关技能，尤其是针灸和草药疗法方面的知识。

column1: Part of the incentive was financial, Dr Laver said. ‘ The bottom line is that most general practitioners are business people.
column2: 拉弗博士表示，其中的一部分激励因素来自经济方面的考虑。‘归根结底，大多数全科医生都是商人而已。’

column1: If they see potential clientele going elsewhere, they might want to be able to offer a similar service.’
column2: 如果他们看到潜在客户流向别处，可能会希望提供类似的服务。

column1: In 1993, Dr Laver and his colleagues published a survey of 289 Sydney people who attended eight alternative therapists’ practices in Sydney.
column2: 在1993年，拉弗博士和他的同事们对悉尼的289名患者进行了调查，这些患者曾到访了悉尼的八家替代疗法诊所。

column1: These practices offered a wide range of alternative therapies from 25 therapists.
column2: 这些诊所由25位治疗师提供各种替代疗法。

column1: Those surveyed had experienced chronic illnesses, for which orthodox medicine had been able to provide little relief.
column2: 被调查的人曾患过慢性疾病，而传统医学对这些疾病的缓解效果非常有限。

column1: They commented that they liked the holistic approach of their alternative therapists and the friendly, concerned and detailed attention they had received.
column2: 他们表示，非常欣赏替代治疗师的整体式服务方式，以及所获得的友善、细心且详细的关怀。

column1: The cold, impersonal manner of orthodox doctors featured in the survey.
column2: 调查中提到正统医生表现出冷漠、缺乏人情味的态度。

column1: An increasing exodus from their clinics, coupled with this and a number of other relevant surveys carried out in Australia, all pointing to orthodox doctors’ inadequacies, have led mainstream doctors themselves to begin to admit they could learn from the personal style of alternative therapists.
column2: 越来越多的患者离开主流医生的诊所，而这项调查和在澳大利亚开展的其他多项相关调查，都指出了常规医疗从业者的不足。这些情况使主流医生自己也开始承认，他们可以借鉴替代疗法从业者与病人相处的方式。
column8: orthodox doctors|n. 常规医疗的医生
column12: personal style|n. 与人相处的方式
column13: alternative therapists|n. 替代疗法从业者

column1: Dr Patrick Store, President of the Royal College of General Practitioners, concurs that orthodox doctors could learn a lot about bedside manner and advising patients on preventative health from alternative therapists.
column2: 英国皇家全科医生学院院长帕特里克·斯托尔博士也认为，传统医学专家可以从替代疗法专业人士那里学到很多关于如何与患者沟通以及提供预防保健建议的知识。

column1: According to the Australian Journal of Public Health, 18% of patients visiting alternative therapists do so because they suffer from musculo-skeletal complaints, 12% suffer from digestive problems, which is only 1% more than those suffering from emotional problems.
column2: 根据《澳大利亚公共卫生杂志》的研究，有18%的患者寻求替代疗法的帮助是因为他们患有肌肉骨骼方面的疾病；而12%的患者则是因为消化问题而寻求帮助。与那些因情绪问题寻求帮助的患者相比，这两类患者的比例仅高出1%。

column1: Those suffering from respiratory complaints represent 7% of their patients, and candida sufferers represent an equal percentage.
column2: 有呼吸系统问题的患者占所有患者的7%，而患有念珠菌感染的患者比例同样为7%。

column1: Headache sufferers and those complaining of general ill health represent 6% and 5% of patients respectively and a further 4% see therapists for general health maintenance.
column2: 患有头痛的患者以及那些抱怨身体不适的患者，分别占所有患者的6%和5%；还有4%的患者则是因为整体健康状况不佳而寻求治疗师的帮助。

column1: The survey suggested that complementary medicine is probably a better term than alternative medicine.
column2: 调查显示，与其称其为‘替代医学’，不如使用‘补充医学’这一术语更为恰当。

column1: Alternative medicine appears to be an adjunct sought in times of disenchantment when conventional medicine seems not to offer the answer.
column2: 替代医学似乎在传统医学无法提供答案时，被当作一种补充手段寻求。
